3802:
** πᾰγιδ-εύω**,
(παγίς) **lay a snare for, entrap**, {{LXX+NT|LXX.1Ki.28.9, NT.Matt.22.15.}}
3807:
** παιδᾰγωγ-ός**, ὁ,
={παιδὸς ἀγωγός}, **slave who went with a boy from home to school and back again**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.75, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 725, “El.” 287, 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.7, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 32.28, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lysis” 208c: coupled with τίτθη, τροφός, [prev. author] “R.” 373c; with ἡγεμών, [prev. work] 467d}}; with διδάσκαλος, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 3.1}}; of Phoenix, as the π. of Achilles, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 390e, etc.}}; Fabius is called the π. of Hannibal, **because he always followed him about**, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Fabius Maximus” 5: _metaphorically_, ὁ νόμος π. εἰς Χριστόν}} **has guided us** until attainment of faith in Christ, {{NT|NT.Gal.3.24}}: generally, **leader**, δημοκρατίας, τυραννίδος, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aratus” 48, “Galb.” 17.}}
3812:
** παιδι-όθεν**,
_adverb_ **from a child**, ἐκ π. {{LXX+NT|LXX.Gen.47.3, NT.Mark.9.21.}}
3818:
**Πακατιανή**, -ῆς, ἡ
Pacatiana, the Western part of the Province of Phrygia, as constituted in 4/A.D.: 1Ti subscr. (Rec.).†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
3826:
** παμ-πληθεί**,
_adverb_ **with the whole multitude, NT.Luke.** 23.18, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 75.9.}}
3828:
**Παμφυλία**, -ας, ἡ
**Pamphylia, a province of Asia Minor**: Act.2:10 13:13 14:24 15:38 27:5.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
3829:

3832:
** πᾰνοικ-ί**
or **πᾰνοικ-εί**, = {πανοικεσίᾳ}, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Eryxias” 392c, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 16.4.13, NT.Act.16.34, etc., variant in LXX.Exo.1.1. (Written -εί in “PGiss.” 75.10 (2nd c.AD), “POxy.” 935.30 (3rd c.AD), etc.)}}
3833:
** πᾰνοπλ-ία**,
_Ionic dialect_ -ιη, ἡ, **suit of armour of a** ὁπλίτης, i.e. shield, helmet, breast plate, greaves, sword, and lance, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|“IG” 12.45.11 (probably), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.114, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 16.29, “SIG” 421.39 (Thermae, 3rd c.BC), etc.}}; γυναῖκα σκευάσαντες πανοπλίῃ {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.60; πανοπλίᾳ παντελεῖ κοσμηθεῖσα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 796c; κοσμήσαντες π. Ἑλληνικῇ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.180; πανοπλίαν ἕστηκ᾽ ἔχουσα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 830; π. ἔχων βαδίζεις [prev. author] “Pl.” 951: in _plural_, π. ἐπάργυροι καὶ κατάχρυσοι 1st c.AD: Onosander (Onasander) Tacticus 1.20: _metaphorically_, ἐνδύσασθε τὴν π. τοῦ θεοῦ NT.Eph.6.11.}}
3840:
** πάντοθεν**,
_adverb_, (πᾶς) **from all quarters, from every side**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.623, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1240 (Lyric poetry), etc.; π. πληθύνομαι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1370}}: in _Ionic dialect_ Prose, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.138, 7.129: rare in _Attic dialect_ (πανταχόθεν being preferred), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Critias” 117e; μὴ π. κέρδαινε 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 625, compare “Mon.” 63; οὐ μόνον κατ᾽ εὐθυωρίαν, ἀλλὰ π. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 656b29; π. λαμβάνειν [prev. author] “EN” 1121b32: frequently with _preposition_, π. ἐκ κευθμῶν 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.28; περὶ γὰρ κακὰ π. ἔστη 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.270: with _genitive_, π. εἰδώλων 4th-3rd c.BC: Aratus Epicus 455}}:—the form **πάντοθε** is only variant in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.225, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 17.97, “Anthologia Graeca” 11.85 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus).—On the accent, see 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 192.2.}}
3841:
** παντο-κράτωρ** [κρᾰ], ορος, ὁ,
**almighty**, of Hermes, {{LXX|“epigram Gr.” 815 (Cretan dialect); Κύριος LXX.2Ki.5.10, +others; θεός Aristeas 125}}; ὁ π. alone, **the Almighty,** {{NT|NT.Rev. 1.8.}}
3842:
** πάντοτε**,
_adverb_ **always**, {{NT+4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 187, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1166a28, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 324, 720; twice in LXX, LXX.Wis.11.21, 19.18, compare “BGU” 1123.8 (1st c.BC), NT.Matt.26.11, +others, “IG” 3.1362, 7.2713, 1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 32.37, etc.: condemned by the Atticists, who recommend διαπαντός or ἑκάστοτε, 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 82, Moer.p.319 P.}}
3851:
** παραβολ-εύομαι**,
**venture, expose oneself**, π. τῇ ψυχῇ NT.Phil.2.30 (variant **παραβουλεύομαι**): with _accusative_ _cognate_, τοὺς ὑπὲρ φιλίας κινδύνους π. {{Refs 4th c.BC+|“IPE” 12.39.28 (Olbia, iii (?) 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator).}}
3864:
** παραθᾰλάσσ-ιος**,
_Attic dialect_ **παραθαλάττιος**, α, ον (also ος, ον {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.56)}}, **beside the sea**, τὰς πόλιας τὰς π. {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.109; τὰς π. κώμας [prev. author] 8.23; τὰ π. τῆς Ἑλλάδος [prev. author] 3.135; τὰ π. τῶν καρπῶν [prev. author] 4.199}}; ἡ π. (i.e. γῆ) {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 4.8.7.}}
3866:
** παρα-θήκη**, ἡ,
**anything entrusted to** one. **deposit**, {{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.86, 9.45, “BGU” 1004.15 (3rd c.BC), LXX.Lev.6.2 (5.21), 1st c.AD(?): Pseudo-Phocylidea 135, “Ostr.Bodl.” i 274 (1st c.BC), “SIG” 742.51 (Ephesus, 1st c.BC)}}; of persons, **hostage**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.73.}}
3871:
** παρα-κᾰλύπτω**,
**cover by hanging something beside, cloak, disguise**, τῇ μέθῃ τὴν διάνοιαν {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Demetrius” 52}}:—_middle_, **cover one's face**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 439e, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alcibiades” 34; πρὸς τὸ δεινόν [prev. author] “Pomp.” 60}} (_active_ in same sense, {{Refs|[prev. author] “Per.” 35): _metaphorically_, παρακαλυπτομένου τοῦ λόγου}} **veiling itself**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 503a, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.370f; π. τὴν ἀλήθειαν 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.196}}; **set aside, ignore**, τὸν θεόν {{Refs|[prev. work] 189.}}
3885:
** παρα-λῠτικός**, ή, όν,
**paralytic,** {{NT+1st c.AD+|NT.Matt.4.24, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.16, 2nd c.AD: Rufus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 8.39.8.}}
3892:
** παρανομ-ία**, ἡ,
**transgression of law, decency**, or **order**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 5.12, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.98, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 537e, etc.}}; ἡ κατὰ τὸ σῶμα π. ἐς τὴν δίαιταν **loose and disorderly habits** of life, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.15, compare 28; π. εἴς τινας 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.6.13; περὶ τὰς σπονδάς 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 8.4}}; **illegality**, personified, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.54.10.}}
3893:
** παραπικρ-αίνω**,
**embitter, provoke**, with _accusative_, {{LXX|LXX.Eze.20.21}}; **rebel against**, τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦ Κυρίου{{LXX|LXX.1Ki.13.26: _absolutely_, LXX.Eze.24.3, +others}}; παραπικραίνουσα παρεπικράνθην{{LXX+NT|LXX.Lam.1.20, cf. NT.Heb.3.16.}}
